documents.title: Gallbladder pill
documents.author: patient
documents.body: The GI doctor started me on ursodiol for the gallstones. Is it ok with my metformin and thyroid pill? Also, is it normal that it's so expensive? The pharmacy said they needed something from insurance.

documents.title: RE: Gallbladder pill
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: No problem with metformin. Take your levothyroxine on its own in the morning as you do now, and the ursodiol with meals. I added it to your list. For the cost, the GI office handles the prior authorization since they prescribed it; I'll have our nurse nudge them.

documents.title: Prior authorization
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called GI office re: ursodiol PA. They submitted 1/9, approved this morning. Pt informed, picking up today.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: R heel pain x 2 months.
HPI: Started after New Year. Worst with the very first steps out of bed - sharp, pulling under the heel and sometimes along the arch. Loosens after she walks a few minutes and she can get through the day with mild ache, but it comes back after she sits and gets up again (lunch, end of reading group). She is on her feet all day in the classroom on a tile floor. No injury. No fevers, no other joints, no numbness. GI saw her in December for gallstones, on ursodiol since, the after-meal discomfort is much better.
Meds: metformin, levothyroxine, ursodiol, MVI, ibuprofen prn (uses it some for the heel).
Exam: BMI 31. R foot: point tender over the medial calcaneal tuberosity. No swelling, redness or warmth. Heel cord nontender. Normal sensation and pulses.
A: Right plantar fasciitis.
P: Calf and plantar fascia stretching sheet, frozen water bottle roll, supportive shoes with a firm heel counter (no flats in class), avoid barefoot at home. Ibuprofen with food as needed, sparingly. Referral to sports medicine since she'd like someone to look at it if not better in a few weeks.

reports.text: Right foot, three views. Bones are normally mineralized. Small plantar calcaneal spur. No fracture or dislocation. Joint spaces preserved. No soft tissue abnormality.
reports.conclusion: Small plantar calcaneal spur. Otherwise normal right foot.

documents.title: Sports Medicine Evaluation
documents.author: orthopedics
documents.body:
Orthopedics & Sports Medicine
Visit: 03/21/2023

Thank you for sending Ms. Pomeroy, 47, with type 2 diabetes, obesity and hypothyroidism, for right plantar foot pain of about three months that has been getting worse. Her pain is most intense with her first morning steps and when she stands after sitting. She teaches and stands for most of the school day, which aggravates it.

Medications: metformin 1000 mg BID, levothyroxine 100 mcg daily, multivitamin, ibuprofen as needed.
Allergies: NKDA. Social: never smoker, no alcohol.

Exam: tenderness to palpation along the anterior plantar calcaneus. Pain reproduced with passive dorsiflexion of the toes (windlass). No swelling. Neurovascularly intact.

Imaging: right foot radiographs today demonstrate a small calcaneal spur, no fracture.

Assessment: right plantar fasciitis; small calcaneal spur, incidental to symptoms.

Plan: continue daily stretching and supportive footwear; over-the-counter arch support; ice; anti-inflammatory as needed with food. Return in 6 weeks.

documents.title: Sports Medicine Follow-up
documents.author: orthopedics
documents.body:
Orthopedics & Sports Medicine follow-up, 05/04/2023

Ms. Pomeroy, now 48, returns for right heel pain present since about early January, roughly four months. Still worst in the morning and after rest, eases somewhat once she has walked a bit, and is worse at the end of long standing days. Over-the-counter acetaminophen and ibuprofen have given her little relief.

Meds: metformin, levothyroxine, multivitamin, ibuprofen as needed. NKDA.

Exam: tender at the anteromedial right calcaneus. Passive dorsiflexion of the toes provokes heel pain. Ankle dorsiflexion and plantar flexion full and painless. No swelling.

Imaging: prior radiographs reviewed, calcaneal spur.

Assessment: right plantar fasciitis, persistent despite home care.

Plan: dorsiflexion night splint; silicone heel cushions in work shoes; formal physical therapy for stretching and strengthening. If not improving in 3 months we can discuss an injection. Follow up as needed.

documents.title: Physical Therapy Initial Evaluation
documents.author: physical therapy
documents.body:
PT Initial Evaluation 5/18/23. Dx: R plantar fasciitis.
Subjective: heel pain since January, 6/10 first steps, 2/10 later in the day. Goal: get through a teaching day without pain.
Objective: tender medial plantar heel. Windlass reproduces pain. Gait normal after warm-up.
Assessment: findings consistent with the referral diagnosis.
Plan: 1x/week x 6 weeks: calf/plantar fascia stretching, intrinsic strengthening, eccentric heel raises, taping trial, HEP. Night splint as prescribed.

documents.body: Discharge after 6 visits (5/18-6/27/23). Morning heel pain now 1/10, none later in the day. Doing her home program on her own. Goals met.

documents.title: Diabetes Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Rescheduled from June. Summer was good, walked most mornings now that her heel is better. Finished PT in late June.
Ursodiol TID - admits she misses the lunchtime dose most school days, better in summer. No belly pain since spring.
Metformin, levo unchanged.
Exam: weight same. Heart and lungs normal. R heel nontender.
A1c and BMP drawn. Physical next month.

documents.title: A1c
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: A1c 7.0, right at the line and a touch higher than last year. Not changing meds; let's see where it is in the winter. Kidney function normal.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
48 y/o F, yearly exam.
Interval: gallstones dx Dec, on ursodiol, no further pain episodes. R plantar fasciitis - PT, night splint, cushions; pain gone since July. Uses the night splint occasionally.
Current meds: metformin 1000 BID, levothyroxine 100 mcg, ursodiol 250 TID, multivitamin, ibuprofen rarely.
ROS: neg. Weight stable.
Exam: Well. Thyroid nonpalpable. Heart: regular, S1S2, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abd soft, NT, no masses. Breasts symmetric, no masses. Feet: intact sensation, pulses good, R heel now nontender. Skin ok.
PHQ-9: 3.
Assessment/plan:
- Plantar fasciitis R: resolved, keep stretching.
- Cholelithiasis on ursodiol: GI repeat US due December.
- DM2: A1c last month 7.0. UACR, lipids today.
- Hypothyroid: TSH.
- HM: FIT returned, mammogram order (due), flu/COVID next month. Colonoscopy vs FIT again discussed, staying with FIT.

documents.title: Immunizations
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Fall vaccines: influenza IM left arm, 2023-24 COVID (Pfizer) IM right arm. VIS reviewed. Observed 15 min, no issues.

reports.text: Bilateral screening mammogram with tomosynthesis, compared to 2022 and 2020. Scattered fibroglandular tissue. No suspicious findings in either breast. Benign-appearing bilateral axillary nodes.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Brought up at the end of a text last week, came in to discuss. About 6 months of leaking urine. Two kinds: a little with coughs and sneezes, and more bothersome, a sudden need to go that she can't always hold - has wet herself a few times before making it to the bathroom, once in the hall at school. Wears a liner daily now. No burning, no blood, not getting up at night to void. Drinks 2 coffees and a diet soda most days.
3 vaginal deliveries. Mom had prolapse.
Dipstick UA in office negative.
Exam: abdomen soft, no suprapubic tenderness.
A: Urinary incontinence, mixed symptoms, urge seems to predominate. UA negative.
P: Referral to gyn (urogyn-trained provider there). Meanwhile cut back caffeine, try to space fluids. Bladder diary sheet given to bring to that appointment.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth three times daily with meals
medications.reason: Gallstones not dissolved after one year

reports.text: Right upper quadrant ultrasound, compared to 12/21/2022. Liver normal in size and echotexture. Gallbladder again contains multiple small shadowing stones, not significantly changed in number or size. Gallbladder wall normal thickness. No pericholecystic fluid. Common bile duct 4 mm. Right kidney unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Persistent cholelithiasis, essentially unchanged. No cholecystitis or ductal dilation.

documents.title: Gastroenterology Follow-up
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Gastroenterology follow-up, 12/12/2023

Ms. Pomeroy returns after one year of ursodiol 250 mg three times daily for gallstones. She has had no further postprandial pain since early in the year. She sometimes missed the midday dose during the school year.

Allergies: NKDA. Medications: metformin, levothyroxine, ursodiol, multivitamin, ibuprofen as needed.

Exam: anicteric, abdomen soft and nontender.

Ultrasound today: multiple small gallstones persist, essentially unchanged from a year ago. No wall thickening, normal bile duct.

Impression: cholelithiasis, now asymptomatic; no response to oral dissolution therapy.

Plan: ursodiol discontinued, since a further year is unlikely to help. I again recommended elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy; she would rather not have surgery while she has no symptoms, and that is a reasonable choice. She will contact her primary physician or us for recurrent pain, fever, jaundice, dark urine or pale stools. Follow up as needed.

documents.title: GI letter
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Got the GI letter. Since the stones didn't shrink they stopped the ursodiol - I've taken it off your list. Agree surgery can wait while you feel well; just let me know right away if the pain comes back or you notice yellowing.

documents.title: RE: GI letter
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Ok thanks. Honestly glad to be done with 3 pills a day. Gyn appt is the 27th.
